case_title: Kusha Duruka v. The State of Odisha
neutral_facts: The accused, Kusha Duruka, and his co-accused, Gangesh Kumar Thakur, were arrested in connection with an allegation that they were in exclusive and conscious possession of 23.8 kg of Ganja and were transporting it. Following their arrest, both filed applications for release on bail pending trial before the Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge, Malkangiri. The Sessions Judge rejected the bail application of the accused. The co-accused filed a bail application before the High Court, which was allowed, while the accused's bail application was dismissed. The accused then filed a special leave petition before the Supreme Court, which was noticed. During the pendency of the matter before the Supreme Court, the High Court granted bail to the accused, but the details of the earlier bail application and the pendency of the special leave petition were not mentioned in the bail application. The Supreme Court directed the High Court to provide the original record of the bail application and to communicate with the Chief Justice and Registrar of the High Court. The High Court provided a report indicating that the State Counsel was not aware of the pendency of the special leave petition and the earlier bail application. The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal as infructuous and imposed a token cost on the accused.
